title: Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
authors: Taylor W. Webb; Keith J. Holyoak; Hongjing Lu
main_finding: Strong GPT-3 performance across multiple analogy tasks launched the modern emergence debate.

title: Large Language Models as Analogical Reasoners
authors: Michihiro Yasunaga; Xinyun Chen; Yujia Li; Panupong Pasupat; Jure Leskovec; Percy Liang; Ed H. Chi; Denny Zhou
main_finding: Self-generating relevant exemplars before solving improves reasoning; analogy used as an inference strategy.

title: StoryAnalogy: Deriving Story-level Analogies from Large Language Models to Unlock Analogical Understanding
authors: Cheng Jiayang et al.
main_finding: 24K story pairs show story-level analogy identification remains difficult; fine-tuning improves generation.

title: ARN: Analogical Reasoning on Narratives
authors: Zhivar Sourati; Filip Ilievski; Pia Sommerauer; Yifan Jiang
main_finding: Near analogies are much easier than far system analogies; few-shot/CoT help but leave a large human gap.

title: AnaloBench: Benchmarking the Identification of Abstract and Long-context Analogies
authors: Xiao Ye; Andrew Wang; Jacob Choi; Yining Lu; Shreya Sharma; Lingfeng Shen; Vijay Murari Tiyyala; Nicholas Andrews; Daniel Khashabi
main_finding: Scaling gives limited gains for long scenarios and retrieval from large story banks.

title: Abstractors and relational cross-attention: An inductive bias for explicit relational reasoning in Transformers
authors: Awni Altabaa; Taylor Webb; Jonathan D. Cohen; John Lafferty
main_finding: Explicit relational attention improves sample efficiency and systematic relational generalization.

title: The relational bottleneck as an inductive bias for efficient abstraction
authors: Taylor W. Webb et al.
main_finding: Frames separation of relational from object-level information as a general inductive bias for abstraction.

title: Evaluating the Robustness of Analogical Reasoning in Large Language Models
authors: Martha Lewis; Melanie Mitchell
main_finding: GPT analogy performance drops sharply under task variants that preserve abstract structure; humans are more robust.

title: KiVA: Kid-Inspired Visual Analogies for Testing Large Multimodal Models
authors: Eunice Yiu; Maan Qraitem; Anisa Noor Majhi; Charlie Wong; Yutong Bai; Shiry Ginosar; Alison Gopnik; Kate Saenko
main_finding: LMMs identify what changed better than how it changed or how to extrapolate the rule; children/adults are much stronger.

title: Self-supervised Analogical Learning using Language Models
authors: Ben Zhou; Sarthak Jain; Yi Zhang; Qiang Ning; Shuai Wang; Yassine Benajiba; Dan Roth
main_finding: Generates surface-distinct cases sharing a reasoning process and uses extracted solution schemas as supervision.

title: Analogical Reasoning Inside Large Language Models: Concept Vectors and the Limits of Abstraction
authors: Gustaw Opiełka; Hannes Rosenbusch; Claire E. Stevenson
main_finding: Some concept representations are invariant and causally steerable; more abstract relations lack stable linear representations.

title: Evidence from counterfactual tasks supports emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
authors: Taylor W. Webb; Keith J. Holyoak; Hongjing Lu
main_finding: Code execution restores performance on shuffled-alphabet variants, showing some failures arise from auxiliary counting/indexing demands.

title: Do large language models solve verbal analogies like children do?
authors: Tamar Johnson; Mathilde ter Veen; Rochelle Choenni; Han van der Maas; Ekaterina Shutova; Claire E. Stevenson
main_finding: LLMs perform strongly but rely heavily on association when relational and associative answers compete.

title: Disentangling and Integrating Relational and Sensory Information in Transformer Architectures
authors: Awni Altabaa; John Lafferty
main_finding: Separate sensory and relational attention channels improve data and parameter efficiency across relational tasks.

title: LLMs as models for analogical reasoning
authors: Sam Musker; Alex Duchnowski; Raphaël Millière; Ellie Pavlick
main_finding: Some LLMs reach human-level accuracy but display different sensitivity profiles, separating human-level from human-like reasoning.

title: Emergent Analogical Reasoning in Transformers
authors: Gouki Minegishi; Jingyuan Feng; Hiroki Furuta; Takeshi Kojima; Yusuke Iwasawa; Yutaka Matsuo
main_finding: Analogical behavior emerges through learnable structural alignment and relation-preserving transformations in Transformer representations.

title: Can LLMs Aid Analogical Reasoning for Strategic Decisions? A Comparative Study
authors: Prothit Sen; Maciej Workiewicz; Phanish Puranam
main_finding: LLMs show high recall but low precision in candidate analogy matching; humans show the reverse profile.

title: The Curious Case of Analogies: Investigating Analogical Reasoning in Large Language Models
authors: Taewhoo Lee; Minju Song; Chanwoong Yoon; Jungwoo Park; Jaewoo Kang
main_finding: Separates missing relational information, application failures, and degraded structural alignment using patching and probes.

title: Enhancing Structural Mapping with LLM-derived Abstractions for Analogical Reasoning in Narratives
authors: Mohammadhossein Khojasteh; Yifan Jiang; Stefano De Giorgis; Frank van Harmelen; Filip Ilievski
main_finding: Combines LLM abstractions with explicit mapping; abstraction-level selection remains a major bottleneck.

title: Human analogical guidance amplifies LLM performance through cross-domain knowledge activation
authors: Rafael Larraz; Avelino Corma
main_finding: Analogical guidance activates remote cross-domain knowledge and enables historically unavailable technical solution generation.

title: Transformer See, Transformer Do: Copying as an Intermediate Step in Learning Analogical Reasoning
authors: Philipp Hellwig; Willem Zuidema; Claire E. Stevenson; Martha Lewis
main_finding: Copying subtasks and heterogeneous meta-training enable strong new-alphabet transfer; learned algorithm can be reconstructed and steered.

title: Can Large Language Models Generalize Analogy Solving Like Children Can?
authors: Claire E. Stevenson; Alexandra Pafford; Han L. J. van der Maas; Melanie Mitchell
main_finding: Children and adults transfer analogy solving to Greek and unfamiliar symbols; tested LLMs largely fail far transfer.

title: Grounding Before Generalizing: How AI Differs from Humans in Causal Transfer
authors: Liangru Xiang; Yuxi Ma; Zhihao Cao; Yixin Zhu; Song-Chun Zhu
main_finding: Models show delayed or absent causal transfer and require environment-specific grounding before transfer gains emerge; humans use abstract causal structure from the first target attempt; visual input often hurts.

title: Unlocking LLM Creativity in Science through Analogical Reasoning
authors: Andrew Shen; Shaul Druckmann; James Zou
main_finding: Cross-domain analogy generation greatly increases diversity and novelty of scientific solution search and yields validated task gains.

title: Learning to Reason by Analogy via Retrieval-Augmented Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
authors: Zilin Xiao; Qi Ma; Chun-cheng Jason Chen; Xintao Chen; Avinash Atreya; Hanjie Chen; Vicente Ordonez
main_finding: Trains retrieval by expected reasoning benefit rather than semantic overlap and couples retrieved analogous reasoning traces to RFT; AIME 2025 avg@32 +7.1/+2.8 over GRPO for Qwen3-1.7B/4B.

title: Modelling Analogies and Analogical Reasoning: Connecting Cognitive Science Theory and NLP Research
authors: Molly R. Petersen; Claire E. Stevenson; Lonneke van der Plas
main_finding: Current synthesis connecting analogy subprocesses to NLP challenges and emphasizing relational over entity-level similarity.

title: CHAIRO: Contextual Hierarchical Analogical Induction and Reasoning Optimization for LLMs
authors: Haotian Lu; Yuchen Mou; Bingzhe Wu
main_finding: End-to-end optimization of analogical retrieval and induced rules improves a real moderation application; evidence is task-specific.

title: Analogical Deep Research: Retrieving and Integrating Historical Analogies for Foresight Analysis
authors: Yongqiang Chen; Guangyi Chen; Yuewen Sun; Kun Zhang
main_finding: Mechanism alignment and cross-analogy confirmation improve open-world analogy retrieval and integration for foresight.

title: On the Diversity of Analogy Making in Large Language Models
authors: Yuanhao Shen; Daniel Xavier de Sousa; Caio César Sifuentes Barcelos; Hongyu Guo; Xiaodan Zhu
main_finding: Generated analogies are domain-homogeneous; increasing diversity often trades off against quality and appears controlled differently across models.

method_family: multi-turn agentic analogical trajectories; trajectory optimization
title: Agentic Analogical Reasoning for Large Language Models
authors: anonymous under double-blind review in public submission
main_finding: Treats analogy as iterative thinking→analogizing→contextualizing; trains generated and reweighted analogical trajectories to internalize multi-turn analogical reasoning; evidence remains submission-stage.
